extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing a Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society using AMS‑LaTeX (memo-l)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and production rules for preparing, formatting, and submitting a Memoirs (monograph) manuscript using the AMS memo-l document class and AMS‑LaTeX packages; covers preamble, top matter, body, floats, graphics, bibliographies, indexing, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the supplied template
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the template supplied in the author package for the Memoirs; this will call the memo-l document class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy the template to a file with a suitable name and use it as the basis for your manuscript so that the AMS class and required tags are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: File names should not exceed 20 characters and consist only of numeric or unaccented alphabetic (ASCII) characters; avoid overly generic names such as chap1.tex, mybib.tex or fig1.eps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose identifying, short ASCII-only names to avoid problems in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify page sizes or dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions; page sizes must conform to the specifications of the Memoirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing text width or other dimensions will change line breaks (critical for math displays, tables, figures) and will be reverted in production, potentially introducing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change default font size
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify the default font size except temporarily for proofreading; the default is [10pt].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using other sizes affects line breaks (esp. displays and inline math); reprocess and check breaks if you use larger sizes during drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only public CTAN packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only 'public' packages available from CTAN (the Comprehensive TeX Archive Network).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packages not publicly available or unsupported by AMS production can cause processing failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid incompatible or problematic packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use packages known to cause production problems (e.g., biblatex, epsfig, diagrams by Paul Taylor, geometry, microtype, makeidx, parskip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a package is not supported by AMS production, avoid it; the handbook lists recommended and discouraged packages with explanations of incompatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended packages
rubrics_metrics.description: The handbook lists packages that are compatible or useful (e.g., amssymb, amsbooka, amsmidx, imakeidx, graphicx, longtable, mathrsfs, mathtools, natbib, upref, tikz, xypic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer these packages for their compatibility and features; templates may include recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place macro definitions in the preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Put definitions for frequently occurring mathematical expressions and any new commands in the preamble (between \documentclass and \begin{document}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove unused commands before submission; include macros explicitly (not entire macro files) so the file can be processed independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define macros with \newcommand, not \def
rubrics_metrics.description: Always use \newcommand; do not use \def.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \newcommand warns you if the name is already in use; do not redeclare existing LaTeX or AMS-LATEX commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redefine LATEX/AMS commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not redeﬁne any existing LATEX or AMS-LATEX commands or commands from amsmath/amscls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redefinitions can break AMS production; use class-provided commands and environments when possible (e.g., use AMS proof environment).

rubrics_metrics.name: No author-defined macros in top-matter fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use author-defined macros in author names, titles, abstract, section and theorem headings, or references; use only standard commands and avoid hard-coded font changes there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author-defined macros in top-matter prevent proper indexing and cause production issues; use coding appropriate for special fonts only within the body text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid math in titles and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using math in the title and in other headings because titles are provided to on-line bibliographic services for indexing; TeX math coding (especially dollar signs) will result in inaccurate bibliographic listings and problematic PDF bookmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If math is necessary, restrict fonts to Computer Modern, amsfonts/amssymb, and mathrsfs; otherwise avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the 2010 MSC numbers for primary and secondary subjects and enter them with \subjclass[2010]{...}. At least one primary classification is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full MSC numbers from www.ams.org/msc; omitting [2010] defaults to 1991 scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include abstract (with suggested length limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoirs must contain an abstract; upper limit suggested about 150 words for short papers and 300 words for long papers (approx.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract may have multiple paragraphs and displays, but must not use author-defined macros, \cite, or \ref; it is used for bibliographic services (e.g., Zentralblatt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge grants with \thanks
rubrics_metrics.description: Give information on grants or contracts (including grant numbers) under which the research was performed using the \thanks command in the top matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \thanks entries appear as unnumbered footnotes at the bottom of the first page; enter \thanks immediately following the address(es) for the relevant author (not within \author{}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide author addresses and contact info in top matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the research address/institutional affiliation (required) and current address (if different), and optionally email and URL for each author using \address, \curraddr, \email, \urladdr commands (addresses not inside \author{}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email addresses appear in online Memoirs; URLs appear in print only in certain contexts; do not abbreviate addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread thoroughly; submitted source must match accepted copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread your Memoir carefully; the files you send must be the EXACT files used to generate the accepted reference copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications in Memoirs will not be given editorial proofreading. Verify all checklist items before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use TeX coding to control line/page breaks or explicit spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not insert TeX coding for line and page breaks or explicit horizontal/vertical spacing commands in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such coding will usually need to be removed for production and can introduce errors; let production handle final pagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbers placed at left (AMS style)
rubrics_metrics.description: For displayed equations, AMS style requires equation numbers to be on the left (flush with left margin) by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Left placement avoids interference with \qed boxes; other numbering styles will be changed to AMS standard in production (risking inadvertent errors). Options like [reqno] are supported but discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \cite for citations (not in abstract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the \cite command to indicate citations; \cite may not appear in an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All references will be replaced in production by amsrefs form drawn from MathSciNet when available; include full bibliographic information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include full reference information and use AMS abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all available information for references and use abbreviations for journals and series from AMS sources; references will be converted to amsrefs drawn from MathSciNet where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare bibliographic data carefully to aid automated conversion and indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS theorem support and declare theorem types in preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS classes include amsthm; activate theorem types in the preamble with \theoremstyle and \newtheorem statements. Three styles are provided: plain (italic), definition (upright), and remark (upright, no extra space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Use 
ewtheorem{thm}{Theorem} or 
ewtheorem{thm}{Theorem}[section] for numbering; use 
ewtheorem{lem}[thm]{Lemma} to share counters; include all 
ewtheorem specs in the preamble and prefer the AMS proof environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem numbering options
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem environments can be numbered consecutively throughout the document or within sections; theorem counters can be tied to other counters (e.g., equation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \newtheorem{thm}{Theorem}[section] or \newtheorem{thm}[equation]{Theorem}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heading levels and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Six heading levels are provided (\part, \chapter, \specialsection, \section, \subsection, \subsubsection); any heading may be labeled with \label{...} directly after the heading and referenced with \ref{...}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references require running LaTeX at least twice to resolve; provide short forms for running heads when needed in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter and running-head capitalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In chapter titles, capitalize the first and last words and all nouns, pronouns, adjectives, adverbs, and verbs; articles, conjunctions, and prepositions are lowercased except when first/last or after a colon. Running heads: left (even) pages have the chapter title in uppercase; right (odd) pages have the (shortened) section title in uppercase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uppercasing of running heads is applied automatically with AMS style files; provide a short running-head form if title is long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \include (not \input) for chapter source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a driver file and put the source for each chapter in a separate file, pulled together with \include (not \input).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports production and separate compilation consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter placement and page organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, every chapter must begin on a new right-hand (odd-numbered) page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the class defaults unless instructed otherwise by AMS production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-matter tag usage and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the AMS top-matter commands (e.g., \title, \author, \address, \subjclass[2010]{...}, \maketitle, \begin{abstract}...\end{abstract}); the template contains required and optional tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill tags as appropriate; some fields (e.g., date, translator) are handled by AMS staff if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributors formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors (e.g., 'with an appendix by ...') use \contrib[bracketed text]{Name} and multiple contributors are combined automatically with appropriate punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide addresses for contributors as for authors; the bracketed portion is required and provides exact printed phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-page unnumbered footnotes: MSC and grant info
rubrics_metrics.description: Unmarked, unnumbered footnotes on the abstract page should include primary classification numbers (2010 MSC) (required); grant information (optional); and keywords (optional). Formatting is automatic with AMS style files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter MSC via \subjclass[2010]{...} and grants via \thanks immediately after relevant addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking for the Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag manuscripts for maximum linking on the Web; an AMS-specific hyperref package will be added by AMS staff to enable internal cross-reference and external URL linking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \label, \ref, \cite, and \eqref per standards; AMS will add and configure hyperref during production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical text coding and roman-type guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical expressions should be coded as math ($...$ or \(...\)); numbers, punctuation, labels, and certain abbreviations should be upright (roman) using \textup{...} where needed; use standard control sequences for functions/operators and \DeclareMathOperator for new operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between mathematical and textual elements (e.g., years, labels). Use upref if needed to force roman for \ref inside non-roman environments; \eqref produces '(n)' in roman type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the xca environment (defined in the preamble with \theoremstyle{definition} and \newtheorem) for exercises that appear individually within a section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The xca environment is used like other theorem-class environments and is encouraged for exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: include index tags and run MakeIndex
rubrics_metrics.description: Include index terms directly in the TeX files for correct page references; use \makeindex in preamble and \printindex where index should appear. MakeIndex must be run separately and LaTeX rerun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the makeidx package; for multiple indexes use amsmidx or imakeidx (with specific options) as documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floats: treatment and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and tables are usually handled as floating inserts; they should be numbered consistently (figures and tables separately), placed at top or bottom, have an in-text reference, and appear within the same section as their first reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A figure/table should not precede its first text reference unless both appear on the same page spread; small integral items may appear unnumbered in place in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hard-setting float placement (avoid [h!])
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow floats to float according to LaTeX defaults preset by the document class; avoid using [h!] which can introduce pagination problems for AMS production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final placement of inserts is determined by AMS production staff based on appropriate page layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption placement conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Caption for a figure is positioned below the figure; caption for a table is positioned above the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the general structure \begin{figure} ... \caption{...} \label{...} \end{figure} and \begin{table} \caption{...} \label{...} ... \end{table}; caption headings (e.g., 'Table 3.1.') are supplied automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Float captions and labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Include caption text as appropriate (may be omitted) and include a \label to refer to the float from the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The style of captions differs from basic LaTeX caption style; reference labels should be unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure graphics do not extend into margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure graphics do not extend into the margins and conform to AMS graphics guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check size, bounding box and placement; excessive extension into margins will cause production problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics file formats and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred formats: EPS (for dvips), TIFF, JPEG; when appropriate, provide TeX-based graphics (tikz, pstricks, xypic) directly in the source; name files according to file-naming rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If TeX graphics code is extensive, put it in a separate file and \input it; when including external graphics, use graphicx and include the correct file name and bounding box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bitmap resolution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs must be at least 300 dpi at the actual printed size; other bitmap graphics have specified resolution requirements depending on content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scale photographs in TeX; prepare images at the size they will be printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics intended to be printed in color should be submitted in CMYK format; RGB files will be converted to CMYK and AMS cannot guarantee exact color match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All color graphics (RGB or CMYK) are analyzed and optimized for printed publication. For grayscale/black-and-white printings, convert and check legibility before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color-to-grayscale conversion guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If color graphics will be printed in black and white/grayscale, they should be converted before submission and checked because lighter colors (yellow) may disappear while other colors may appear similar when converted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check figures on a black-and-white printer to ensure legibility of all elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum width and visibility for colored lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Colored lines should be no less than .5 point in width; colored lines in light colors should be at or near 100% tint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Light-tint lines (e.g., yellow, cyan) can be almost invisible unless at full or near-full intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type in graphics: minimum size and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic type size in graphics should be no less than 10 point at 100%; do not put type on a dark background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10-point type may be hard to read on screen (72 PPI); ensure legibility both on-screen and in print; check conversion to black-and-white as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: width and caption location
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure tables do not exceed the width of the text block; set table captions above the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very wide tables can be rotated with the rotating package and sidewaystable environment; rotate so the left-hand side after rotation is at the bottom of the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph file format and color mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs should be at least 300 dpi at printed size and can be in EPS, TIFF, or JPEG; color photographs must be saved in CMYK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scale photographs in TeX; prepare them at intended print size and color mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using TeX graphics systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use TeX-native graphics systems (tikz/PGF, pstricks, xy/xypic) for diagrams and drawings; tikz recommended for charts and commutative diagrams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of compatibility concerns (pstricks with pdfLaTeX) and include documentation or separate files for extensive code; prefer packages that work in the AMS production environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying labels to graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Labeling packages ensure consistent fonts but labels placed outside graphic edges can extend into margins; if labels extend beyond boundaries add extra space with \vspace to compensate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check final layout to prevent overprinting surrounding material; be cautious when labels lie outside graphic bounding box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission: send only needed files; bundle multiple files
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, send only files needed to process or archive the submission (TeX source, graphics); if multiple files, bundle them with Zip so only one compressed file is sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sending .log or .aux files; bundling reduces chance of name conflicts or corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission method: AMS web server
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted electronic manuscripts should be submitted via the AMS web server (www.ams.org/submit-book-journal); submission requires an AMS web account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors without accounts will be able to create one during submission; web submission is preferred for security and confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Files sent by email should be attached (not in the message body) to pub-submit@ams.org; include the publication code in the subject line to identify the submission as a Memoirs item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions by email are acknowledged automatically; problems with files will be notified via reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate submission options and help
rubrics_metrics.description: If web and email submission fail, arrangements can be made to post files via FTP or on physical media; request help from AMS Technical Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact info and procedures are provided; see the handbook chapter on resources for contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement is sent to authors when the accepted work is received at the AMS; production begins once the signed form is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain certain reuse rights and may be asked (but not required) to transfer other rights to the AMS; copyright transfer details (e.g., public-domain dedication after 28 years) are explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS will add hyperref and do some automated processing
rubrics_metrics.description: An AMS-specific version of hyperref and other production steps (e.g., conversion of bibliographic data to amsrefs form from MathSciNet) will be added by AMS staff at appropriate production stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not load conflicting hyperref versions or bibliography systems unsupported by AMS production; prepare files to be amenable to automated processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and multiple-index support
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple indexes use amsmidx or imakeidx with prescribed options; the AMS document classes include \makeindex and related tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amsmidx syntax or imakeidx with [original] option to preserve AMS formatting; follow given examples to identify index entries and print indexes in backmatter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman type for labels and short textual elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers, punctuation, brackets, braces and symbols used as labels should ideally be set in roman (upright) type even within italic theorem statements; inline mathematical expressions must be coded as math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \textup{...} for roman text inside potentially non-roman environments; distinguish abbreviations/text from variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation breaks and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Check displayed equations to ensure they are broken and aligned following the guidelines (e.g., Swanson) and that they do not exceed the page width; use amsmath structures for multiline displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly broken equations will be corrected in production; authors should ensure correct alignment and width in submitted files.
